Who does what

RoleWhat they do
AdminManages users and every project. Also the product owner (PO) who answers questions about requirements.
QACreates projects, writes and imports test cases, runs them and records results, reviews AI drafts.
DeveloperReviews failures, joins the discussion on a case and marks fixes ready for retest.

Reading the pictures

The numbered marks 1 on each screenshot match the list under it. You may not see every part: some are only for certain roles, and some appear only when there is something to show.

1

Signing in

Sign in with your email address or your username, and your password. Your account is created by an Admin, who gives you a temporary password; you can also create an account yourself, which starts with the QA role.

Sign in

  1. Open WeTestCase in your browser.
  2. Under Email or username, type either one — for example quinn or quinn@company.com. Capital letters do not matter in a username.
  3. Type your password and choose Sign in.
Good to know
  • Forgot your password? Ask an Admin: they can set a new one from Users. There is no email reset.
  • If you see “That account has been disabled”, an Admin has switched your account off.

2

Finding your way around

Every page has the same frame: the menu on the left, and the bell and your account at the top right. On a phone, the menu is behind the ☰ button.

  1. 1
    Dashboard — Progress across every project.
  2. 2
    Projects — Where the work lives: each project's test cases, requirements, runs and reports.
  3. 3
    Users — Admins only: add people, set roles, reset passwords.
  4. 4
    User guide — This guide: read it in the app, or download the PDF.
  5. 5
    Notifications — Answers to your questions, replies to your comments, and fixes ready to retest. A number shows how many are unread.
  6. 6
    Your account — Profile, password, Claude subscription and the on-screen guide.
Good to know
  • The first time you open each page, a short on-screen guide points out its parts. Show the guide in the account menu plays it again.

3

Dashboard

The page you land on after signing in: how testing is going across all the projects you can see.

  1. 1
    The numbers — Projects, test cases, and how many passed, failed, are blocked or have not been run — counting each case's latest result.
  2. 2
    Progress over time — The share of cases run so far, and how many results were recorded each day of the last two weeks (re-runs included).
  3. 3
    Project progress — The five projects with the most cases and how far each has got. Click one to open it.
  4. 4
    Recent activity — The latest results: which case, who recorded it and when.

4

Projects

All the projects you can see. QA and Admins create projects; Developers see the projects they are in charge of.

  1. 1
    New project — Create a project.
  2. 2
    Find a project — Search by name, description or version, and filter by status.
  3. 3
    Cards or table — Show the projects as cards, or as a table.
  4. 4
    Your projects — Each with its status, version and progress. Click a project to open it; the ••• menu edits or deletes it.

Create a project

  1. Choose New project.
  2. Enter the name, and optionally a description and version.
  3. Pick the platforms it is tested on (Web, Android, iOS, API…), its status and dates.
  4. Choose the product owner (PO) — the person who answers questions about requirements — and the people in charge.
  5. Save. Next, add its environments and test cases.

5

A project

A project's overview: its details, where testing stands, and the way to each of its pages.

  1. 1
    Test cases — The project's cases: write, import, run and record results.
  2. 2
    Requirements — The spec, the requirements read from it, and AI-drafted cases to review.
  3. 3
    Failed & blocked — Everything waiting for a fix or a retest; the number shows how many.
  4. 4
    Automation — Run scripted cases in a browser.
  5. 5
    Environments — Where the project is tested, and the default.
  6. 6
    Export — Download a PDF report of the results to share.
Good to know
  • The line under the title shows the default environment, the PO and the people in charge. Below are the project's numbers, its modules and their progress.

6

Test cases

Every test case in the project, with its type, priority, platform and latest result.

  1. 1
    New test case — Write a case by hand.
  2. 2
    Excel — Import cases from an Excel sheet, download the template, or export the list (with the filters you have on).
  3. 3
    Explore the app — Web projects: the AI walks through the app and suggests cases for what it finds.
  4. 4
    Copy to project — Copy cases and their scripts into another project. Results and comments stay; the copies start as Not run.
  5. 5
    Search and filter — Search by TC ID, title or steps; filter by module, status, and more under Filters.
  6. 6
    The cases — Click a case to open it. Tick several to change their module together or move them to the Trash. Sort by a column heading.

Write a test case

  1. Choose New test case.
  2. Give it a TC ID (for example TC-LOGIN-005) and a module — pick one or type a new one. A sub-module is optional.
  3. Choose the test type, priority and platform.
  4. Write the title, preconditions, steps (one per line) and expected result.
  5. Save. The case starts as Not Run.

Import from Excel

  1. Open Excel and choose the import. Download the template first if you do not have one.
  2. Fill one row per case, keeping the template's columns.
  3. Upload the file and check the preview of what will be added, then import.

7

A test case

One case: what to do, what should happen, and everything that has happened to it — results, discussion and the fix.

  1. 1
    Record result — Record what happened when you ran it.
  2. 2
    Previous and next — Move through the list without going back to it.
  3. 3
    The case — Preconditions, steps and expected result, with Edit and the requirement it covers.
  4. 4
    Fix status — On a failed case: who is fixing it and how far it has got.
  5. 5
    Discussion — Comments, files and questions for the PO.
  6. 6
    History — Every result recorded, newest first.

Record a result

  1. Choose Record result.
  2. Pick Passed, Failed or Blocked, and the environment under Tested on.
  3. For Failed or Blocked, describe the actual result — what happened instead.
  4. Add a comment and attach screenshots or a video if they help.
  5. Save. The result goes into the history and the case's status changes.

Get a failure fixed

  1. QA records the case as Failed; it appears on Failed & blocked.
  2. A Developer sets the fix status to Investigating, then Fixed — ready for retest (or Won't fix / Not a bug).
  3. QA is notified, chooses Start retesting, runs the case again and records the new result.

Discuss and ask the PO

  1. Under Discussion, write a comment; attach files with the paperclip. Enter sends, Shift+Enter starts a new line.
  2. Choose Reply under a comment to answer it.
  3. When the expected behaviour is unclear, ask the PO: the comment box turns into a question and its button reads Ask the PO. When the PO answers, you are offered to update the case with the answer.
Good to know
  • The ✨ button beside a comment box fixes spelling and grammar with the AI. You read the result before posting, and can undo it.

8

Requirements

Turn the product spec into test cases: upload the PRD or FRD, check the requirements the AI reads from it, and review the cases it drafts. Every case keeps a link to the requirement it covers.

  1. 1
    Coverage — Requirements, how many are verified and covered by cases, and drafts waiting for review.
  2. 2
    Requirements, Review drafts, Documents — The three steps of the work, one tab each.
  3. 3
    Ask AI — Ask about the requirements and drafts — what is not covered yet, what changed, what to check next.

From a document to test cases

  1. Under Documents, upload the PRD or FRD — PDF, Word, Excel, Markdown, text or HTML. The AI reads it into requirements.
  2. Under Requirements, read each one and choose Verify when it is right. Fix or ask about the ones that are not.
  3. Ask the AI to draft cases for verified requirements.
  4. Under Review drafts, accept the good drafts — they become test cases linked to their requirement — and reject the rest.

When a requirement is unclear

  1. Choose Ask the PO on the requirement and write the question.
  2. The PO is notified and answers in the thread. Resolve the question once it is settled.
Good to know
  • When a new version of a document is uploaded, changed requirements are marked, and the cases linked to them show a notice so they can be checked.
  • The AI features run on your own Claude subscription — connect it once under your account.

9

Failed & blocked

Every case whose latest result is Failed or Blocked, grouped by test type: the list developers work through.

  1. 1
    Export — Download the list as a report for the developers.
  2. 2
    What needs fixing — Each case with its latest result, the actual result, comments, screenshots and fix status. Open one to work on it.

10

Automation

Run the Web and API cases that have a Playwright script, against one of the project's environments. Results land on the cases with screenshots and traces.

  1. 1
    At a glance — How many cases have a script, how the last run went, and the environments.
  2. 2
    New run — Choose the cases and an environment, and start a run.
  3. 3
    Download all scripts — Every script as a Playwright project, to run outside WeTestCase.
  4. 4
    Runs — Every run and how it went. Open one to watch it live or see what failed.

Automate a case

  1. Open a Web or API case and, under Automation, write its Playwright script — or let the AI write it.
  2. Back on Automation, choose New run, pick the cases and the environment, and start it.
  3. Open the run to watch it live. Each case's result is recorded on the case.
Good to know
  • Runs need an environment and the runner switched on for the server; the page says so when either is missing.

11

Environments

Where the project is tested — for example SIT and UAT — with their web and API addresses, start page and test accounts.

  1. 1
    Add an environment — Its name, base URLs, start page and test variables.
  2. 2
    Set as default — The default is chosen in advance wherever an environment is asked for.

12

Trash

Deleted test cases wait here, with their history, comments and scripts, until someone restores them or deletes them for good. Their TC IDs stay taken meanwhile.

  1. 1
    Deleted cases — Tick cases to restore them, or delete them forever.

13

Users (Admins)

Admins manage who can sign in and what they can do.

  1. 1
    Add user — Create an account: name, username, email, temporary password and role.
  2. 2
    The team — Search; each row's ••• menu edits the person, resets their password, disables or deletes the account.

Add someone

  1. Choose Add user.
  2. Enter the full name, a username, the email and a temporary password (at least 8 characters).
  3. Choose the role — Admin, QA or Developer — and create the account.
  4. Give them their username or email and the temporary password; they can change the password after signing in.
Good to know
  • A disabled account keeps its history but cannot sign in. You cannot disable yourself, and one active Admin must always remain.

14

Your account

Open the menu under your name at the top right.

  • Profile — your photo, name and username. Click the photo to crop it; the camera button changes or removes it (a removal happens when you save, and can be undone until then).
  • Change password — enter the current one, then the new one twice.
  • Claude subscription — connect your own Claude Pro or Max plan; every AI feature runs on it. The steps for Mac and Windows are on that screen.
  • Show the guide — play the on-screen guide for the page you are on.
  • Sign out.
